title: the Rajasuya
hook: Krishna arrives, hears the plan, and names the one king who stands in the way: Jarasandha of Magadha

segments.voice: Yesterday: everyone in the sabha said yes, and Yudhishthira sent for Krishna anyway. Your line was send for the one who sees further.
screen: `SEND FOR THE ONE WHO SEES FURTHER.`

segments.voice: Krishna comes straight from Dwaraka, and Yudhishthira lays it all out. My father's wish. The sacrifice. My ministers say yes, my brothers say yes. But you'll tell me the truth: should I perform the Rajasuya? And Krishna does. You have every quality it takes, he says. Then comes the but. There's a king in Magadha. While he lives, this can't be done.
screen: `KRISHNA COMES.` → `SHOULD I DO THIS?` → `YES. BUT THERE'S A KING IN MAGADHA.`

segments.voice: First, what Yudhishthira is asking for. The Rajasuya is the great royal sacrifice, the one Harishchandra performed. A king who completes it is honored by other kings as sovereign over them, so it can't be done alone. Other rulers have to come, and bow, and bring gifts. That's exactly the problem Krishna names. The king is Jarasandha of Magadha. In Krishna's telling, many kings already bow to him. Worse, he has captured kings in battle and holds them shut up in his mountain city, meaning to offer them as a sacrifice to Mahadeva. While those kings sit in his prison, Krishna says, no one else can claim to be honored by the kings of the earth. And Krishna tells it as someone hurt by it. Fearing Jarasandha, he says, my own people, the Yadavas, left Mathura and went to live at Dwaraka. He's not posing as untouchable; he's telling the king plainly what this enemy cost his own family. Look at what his counsel does. It doesn't say yes, and it doesn't say no. It changes the question. Yudhishthira asked, should I perform the sacrifice? Krishna answers: first, what about the kings in that prison? In Krishna's hands the Rajasuya stops being a ceremony for one king's glory and becomes a road through a locked gate. Before anyone can be honored, someone has to be set free. Tomorrow, Yudhishthira very nearly gives the whole thing up.
screen: `A SACRIFICE THAT MAKES A SOVEREIGN.` · `JARASANDHA OF MAGADHA.` · `KINGS LOCKED IN HIS CITY.` · `KRISHNA'S PEOPLE LEFT MATHURA.` · then, large: `FIRST, SOMEONE HAS TO BE SET FREE.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind something you want to do or build, and hold it lightly. Then ask, the way Krishna does, what stands in the way: not to talk yourself out of it, just to see the road honestly, and whether something has to be cleared, or someone helped, first. Let it show itself, and breathe beside it.
The Rajasuya. The great royal sacrifice that makes a king sovereign over kings, and that Krishna says can't happen while Jarasandha holds kings captive.
Your line: a king in Magadha. Before the honor, a prison door. Day seven hundred fifty-two, done.

howItsDone: The Rajasuya belongs to the Vedic royal rites; in the Mahabharata, Yudhishthira's Rajasuya is the rite through which other kings recognize his rule at Indraprastha.

chat.says: Krishna said Yudhishthira could perform the Rajasuya. So why the delay?
options: While Jarasandha held kings captive, no one else could be honored by the kings.
Krishna said the stars weren't right, and the rite must wait a year.
Yudhishthira's brothers refused to ride out until Krishna's army came.
chat.meaning: Krishna said Yudhishthira had every quality it takes, but while Jarasandha of Magadha held kings captive, the Rajasuya couldn't be done.

Jarasandha.meaning: king of Magadha, who held captured kings in prison

Magadha.meaning: Jarasandha's kingdom, ruled from a mountain city

Mahadeva.meaning: the great god, a name of Shiva

Mathura.meaning: the city the Yadavas left for Dwaraka

sources.ref: Mahabharata, Sabha Parva, Rajasuyarambha Parva (Krishna's arrival and counsel; Jarasandha and the captive kings; the Yadavas leave Mathura)

notes: All paraphrase. Confirm Krishna's statement that Yudhishthira has the qualities for the Rajasuya but cannot perform it while Jarasandha lives.
Confirm that Krishna says Jarasandha holds captured kings in Girivraja intending to sacrifice them to Mahadeva (Rudra), and that the Yadavas left Mathura for Dwaraka out of fear of him.
The definition of the Rajasuya (consecration as sovereign over kings) is general; no etymology is given on purpose.
